CVE-2026-116566: socket.getaddrinfo() accepted embedded null bytes in its host and port arguments and silently truncated them at the first null. Upstream fixed it on the main branch in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/160898 (https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/131a3a66c5f400b588f9fd2732a5ed4e89623ee3), first released in the CPython 3.16.0a2 pre-release; no CPython 3.12 release carries the fix. See https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-116566. Checked the _socket extension module for the 'getaddrinfo() host must not contain null characters' check the fix adds in the python-3.12 package of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 3.12.12-r0 to 3.12.16-r4, x86_64 and aarch64; both architectures agree. 3.12.16-r4 is the first build that carries a backport of the upstream change, and every earlier build lacks it. The range ends at 3.12.16-r4.

CVE-2026-116566: socket.getaddrinfo() accepted null bytes in its host and port arguments, which could silently truncate them. Upstream fixed it on the main branch in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/160898 (https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/131a3a66c5f400b588f9fd2732a5ed4e89623ee3; https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/HCHE62VYTPYI6WOPJQDWUBR4CINBPSM7/); no CPython 3.14 release carries it yet and the CVE record names no fixed 3.14 version; https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-116566. Checked the _socket extension module in every published build, 3.14.3-r0 to 3.14.10-r4, of the DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.14 package on x86_64 and aarch64 for the check the fix adds to getaddrinfo() (its 'host must not contain null characters' error). 3.14.3-r0 to 3.14.10-r3 lack the fix; 3.14.10-r4 is the first published build that has it and carries a DHI backport of the upstream fix, and every later build carries it.

The fix (https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/131a3a66c5f400b588f9fd2732a5ed4e89623ee3) was backported to the 3.15 branch in https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/160925 after the 3.15.2 release. This owner carries an adapted backport from 3.15.2-r4 for Alpine 3.23: the _socket extension in 3.15.2-r4 on x86_64 and aarch64 contains the new null-character errors, and those in 3.15.0-r0 and 3.15.2-r0 through 3.15.2-r3 do not. Pending: the affected versions also match the component versions 3.15.0 and 3.15.2 without a package revision, and 3.15.2 covers builds on both sides of the fix, so no version range classifies it correctly. The status will be set once the affected versions are re-evaluated against package-level builds.

CVE-2026-116566: socket.getaddrinfo() accepted null bytes in its host and port arguments, which could silently truncate them. Upstream fixed it on the main branch in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/160898 (https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/131a3a66c5f400b588f9fd2732a5ed4e89623ee3; https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/HCHE62VYTPYI6WOPJQDWUBR4CINBPSM7/); no CPython 3.14 release carries it yet and the CVE record names no fixed 3.14 version; https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-116566. Checked the _socket extension module in every published build, 3.14.5-0 to 3.14.10-6, of the DHI Debian 13 python-3.14 packages (the standard library is in libpython-3.14-minimal and libpython-3.14, or libpython-3.14-stdlib in the earliest builds) on amd64 and arm64 for the check the fix adds to getaddrinfo() (its 'host must not contain null characters' error). 3.14.5-0 to 3.14.10-2 lack the fix; 3.14.10-3 is the first published build that has it and carries a DHI backport of the upstream fix, and every later build carries it.
